note: Binding-layer fixtures are intentionally unimplemented: the public call shape of the engine is still being redesigned. Each entry names a semantic fixture id and the calling shapes the frozen contract must expose before it can run.

shapes.prepared-parameters: Bind ? placeholders to values without string interpolating the SQL text.
shapes.cursor-iterate: Read one row at a time and observe the value stream rather than a preallocated array.
shapes.transaction: Wrap several statements so a rejected statement rolls the whole unit back.
shapes.exec-multi-statement: Run a semicolon-separated script and receive one result per statement.
shapes.affected-count: Report how many rows a mutating statement touched.
shapes.error-detail: Receive a structured code, message, clause and position instead of a bare throw.
shapes.typed-columns: Receive declared column names and storage classes alongside the row values.

cases.expect: same rows as `SELECT a FROM t1 WHERE b = 3`
same rows as `SELECT a FROM t1 WHERE b BETWEEN 2 AND 3`
same rows as `SELECT a FROM t1 ORDER BY a LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1`
rows arrive in the same order and with the same declared columns as the eager result
stopping iteration early neither errors nor hides the remaining rows of a new query
one inserted row reported, and the rowid alias read back as `a`
a structured rejection naming the violated constraint rather than a message-only throw
the failed insert leaves `count(*)` at zero and releases the transaction cleanly
one result object per statement, in script order
the failing `CREATE TABLE` is reported and the follow-up `SELECT` still rejects as unknown table
a bound blob reads back as the same bytes and reports the blob storage class
each row reports the storage class it actually holds, not the declared affinity
a comparison against a bound null yields no row rather than an error
a script creating sixty tables commits all of them before the final count
